page: Microsoft Azure M176bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by Microsoft Hyper-V and dedicated fourth-generation Intel Xeon 8473C processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 176 vCPUs across 88 physical cores running at up to 4.0 GHz with two threads per core. The underlying processor architecture features 105 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache, accompanied by Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction support. Memory capacity is sized at 1536.0 GB of RAM, yielding an allocation ratio of 8.73 GB of system memory per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage, relying entirely on remote Azure Premium Storage and managed block storage volumes, and does not contain discrete hardware GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate exceptional parallel processing and memory throughput. The system reaches top-decile multi-core compute marks, logging 141597.68 on stress-ng and 117452.65 on PassMark CPU, alongside a clang compilation score of 61438.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth achieves 433.27 GB/sec with write throughput reaching 181.68 GB/sec. These high-throughput memory channels enable 171.63 million Redis SET operations per second and 124.71 GB/sec of static web serving throughput. PassMark database operations register at 34000.33, placing in the top ten percent of tested cloud hardware. Single-core results are comparatively moderate, with stress-ng single-core recording 2044.38 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 13.48 GB/sec.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance offers high resource density for enterprise workloads requiring massive RAM footprints combined with extreme thread concurrency. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage requires all persistent data paths to utilize network-attached storage, which introduces latency and throughput dependencies on attached storage configurations. In-memory data persistence, large relational databases, SAP HANA deployments, massive caching tiers, and multi-threaded data transformation jobs represent the primary target workloads for this configuration.
